newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian population falls as economic crisis bites.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian population falls as economic crisis bites.

text.p: A low birth rate and high emigration are making Bulgarians almost an endangered species officials warned on Thursday.
The impoverished Balkan nation's population is expected to fall by 1.3 million by 2020, they said.
"There is a close link between the demographic crisis and the social and economic situation in the country," Zahari Karamfilov, chairman of the National Statistics Institute, told reporters.
"Bulgaria's population of 8.4 million at the end of 1995 is expected to fall to 7.5 million in the year 2010 and to 7.1 million in the year 2020," he said.

Bulgaria has the second lowest birth rate in Europe -- in 1995 it was 8.6 per 1,000 -- which cannot keep pace with the number of deaths, Karamfilov said. Only Latvia lags behind with a birth rate of 8.5 per 1,000.
In the first seven months of this year the birth rate fell further to 8.2 per 1,000. This compares with a death rate of 13.6 per 1,000 for 1995.
Some 580,000 people left Bulgaria between 1989 and 1995, looking for a better life abroad, the Institute's figures show.
In 1989, some 218,000 ethnic Turks left for neighbouring Turkey after the former communist regime banned them from using Moslem names and practising their religion.

"The others who left the country during these years are mainly young and well-educated people, who are looking for a better future in countries such as Canada, the U.S. and South Africa," said Foreign Ministry official Georgi Peichinov.

Bulgarians who remain must struggle with fuel and bread shortages, bank closures, a collapsing currency and monthly inflation approaching 20 percent. The average monthly salary in Bulgaria is now worth the equivalent of $55.
The International Monetary Fund has postponed a badly- needed $115 million credit because of delays in economic reforms pledged by the ruling Socialists.

Two Bulgarian comedians running in presidential elections on October 27, Ivan Koulekov and Hristo Boichev, said they had hoped to meet the Bulgarian people during campaigning on Thursday but couldn't find any.
